findings.title: Duplicate method definition silently replaces the previous `downsize` signature
findings.body: Ruby does not support method overloading. The second definition of `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` on line 149 completely replaces the first definition `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` on line 145. Any existing callers using the old 4-argument form (e.g., `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, out, 100, 200)`) will now have `max_width` interpreted as `dimensions` and `max_height` interpreted as `opts`, producing incorrect behavior or errors. The old method should either be removed entirely (if no callers remain) or kept under a different name.

findings.title: `tempfile.size` will not reflect changes made by the external `convert` process
findings.body: The while loop checks `tempfile.size` to decide whether to keep downsizing. However, `Tempfile#size` returns the size via `fstat` on the file descriptor that was opened when the Tempfile was created. `OptimizedImage.downsize` invokes ImageMagick's `convert` as a subprocess writing to the same path. ImageMagick typically writes to a temporary file and renames it over the target, which means the tempfile's file descriptor still points to the old (now unlinked) inode. As a result, `tempfile.size` will never decrease, the loop will always run all 5 iterations without effect, and the feature will not actually downsize the upload. Use `File.size(tempfile.path)` after each iteration, or re-stat the path, to get the actual on-disk size.

findings.title: No check on `OptimizedImage.downsize` return value before continuing the loop
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` when the image processing fails (e.g., ImageMagick error, unsupported format). The loop does not check this return value, so if downsizing fails on the first attempt, it will silently retry 4 more times, wasting time and resources before proceeding to upload the unmodified file. The loop should break if `downsize` returns false.

findings.title: Client-side max file size is hardcoded to 10 MB, ignoring the admin-configurable site setting
findings.body: The original code read `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, allowing administrators to configure per-type upload limits. Replacing this with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` means the client will permit uploads up to 10 MB regardless of the server's configured limit. Users will be able to select files that the server will reject, producing a confusing experience, and the error message will incorrectly state the limit is 10 MB even when the server enforces a different value.

findings.title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10 MB, bypassing `max_image_size_kb` setting
findings.body: The original code used `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` as the download size limit for URL-based uploads via the API. This is now hardcoded to `10.megabytes`. If an admin has configured a smaller `max_image_size_kb`, the server will still download up to 10 MB from the remote URL before the downsize loop attempts to reduce it. This wastes bandwidth and memory, and if the downsize loop fails (as noted above), oversized files could be stored.
